qs.q: A patient with chronic kidney disease receives a transfusion and develops hypotension and tachycardia 30 minutes later. Urinalysis shows no hemoglobin. Which mechanism is most likely responsible for this acute reaction?
o: Anaphylaxis due to IgA deficiency in the recipient
Activation of complement by incompatible donor antigens
Bacterial contamination of the stored red blood cells
Febrile non-hemolytic reaction from leukocyte antibodies
Citrate toxicity causing acute hypocalcemia symptoms
qs.e: IgA-deficient patients can form anti-IgA antibodies, leading to anaphylaxis upon exposure to IgA-containing blood products.
